This innovative individual, as part of the Product Management team, will be responsible for providing daily and ongoing product and project support, including new product development coordination, product documentation, and collateral and label development. The Product Specialist Intern will collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product launches, organize product information, and assist with product-related issues.

This position reports to the Senior Product Manager. This role is onsite and is based in Fort Myers, Florida.

Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities

- Assist the Product Management team with product documentation, label creation, and marketing collateral updates.
- Support cross-functional teams during new product development by tracking tasks and maintaining project timelines.
- Collaborate with Engineering and Product Development to support new product launches and help keep projects on schedule and within budget.
- Gather and organize product data, including specifications, product requirements, and feedback from internal teams.
- Update databases and collect information to support the development of business cases.
- Help identify and report product-related issues, working closely with Engineering and Customer Support.
- Create product documentation and sales collateral for sales and technical presentations.
- Support dashboard development and data analysis to help the team monitor product performance.
- Learn and apply foundational product management principles under the guidance of the Senior Product Manager.
- Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the Senior Product Manager or Company management.
- Demonstrate integrity, accountability, continuous improvement, and transparency by maintaining accurate product information, taking ownership of assigned tasks, identifying process improvements, and clearly communicating project updates.

Required Qualifications

- Current student (sophomore, junior or senior status).
- Pursuing a degree in Engineering, Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field.
- Technical competency in understanding and preparing documentation for technical systems.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
- Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact.
- Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment.
- Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments.
- Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable.
- Must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship now or in the future.
- Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks and required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

- Engineering focus with a minor in Marketing or Business.
- Interest in gaining experience in Product Management.
- Familiarity with Microsoft Teams and SharePoint.
- Experience with or exposure to Power BI, dashboard development, and data analysis through coursework, academic projects, or previous internships.

General Applicable Company Competencies

- Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency.
- Punctuality and dependability.
- Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions.
- Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts.
- Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees.

Pay Range: $21-27

As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

As a Software Engineering Intern, you’ll join a growing, diverse, and mission-driven team building a new cloud infrastructure from the ground up and work at the forefront of distributed system technologies. You’ll have the opportunity to work on a range of projects across our platform that enables innovation in computationally intensive fields including artificial intelligence, graphics rendering and computational biology.

You’ll collaborate with other engineers to build and maintain scalable and highly available fault-tolerant distributed systems at scale, build products and tools from the ground up that will be used by customers around the world, triage bugs and solve issues in production, and work with product owners and other stakeholders to iterate on new features.

What You'll Be Working On:

Software Engineering Interns may work within one of these three organizations based on your interest and business needs:

Product focused — Cloud Engineering Customer Experience (CCX)

- We build the parts of Crusoe Cloud that customers actually use: the UI they log into, the command-line tool they type into, and the APIs their code talks to. You'll ship features that real customers use before your internship ends.

- Good fit if you like: full-stack or backend web development. Languages: Go, TypeScript/React.

Systems focused — Cloud Availability

- Crusoe runs tens of thousands of GPUs, and our job is keeping them all healthy — mostly by writing software that detects and fixes problems automatically instead of waking someone up at 3am. You'll build tools that replace manual work at real scale.

- Good fit if you like: automation, scripting, and figuring out why things break. Languages: Go and Python.

Infra focused — Cloud Infrastructure

- We build the layer everything else runs on — the compute, storage, and networking that turn racks of servers into a cloud, plus Crusoe Managed Kubernetes, the product customers use to run containers on our GPUs. Work ranges from operating-system-level code to building Kubernetes controllers and operators.

- Good fit if you like: operating systems, distributed systems, or Kubernetes. Languages: mostly Go.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

- Educational Background: You are currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field preferably graduating between Fall 2027 and Spring 2028.

- Programming: You are familiar with coding in a language such as Python, Java, C++, JavaScript, Rust, Go, etc.

- Foundational Knowledge: You're familiar with computer science fundamentals, including data structures and algorithm design.

- Collaborative Mindset: You are a proactive communicator who enjoys working closely with a team to solve challenging problems.

- Problem-Solving Skills: You have a curious and analytical mindset with a talent for troubleshooting and optimizing complex systems.

About the Systems Modeling Team

The Systems Modeling Team has tremendous power to shape Zipline’s products. We develop physics-based models and use them to architect our aircraft, as well as the supporting logistics system. Using simulation, we can rapidly explore a vast array of designs to optimize future products, and we can find ways to squeeze more performance out of our existing products.

Systems Modeling brings diverse teams and fields together (e.g. electrical, thermal, mechanical, aerodynamics, battery chemistry, controls, fleet operations, economics) to gain new insights. Leading the way in drone delivery requires pushing the limits of individual component technologies and carefully orchestrating which ones we put together to optimize the performance of the complete vehicle. How much of the benefit of a larger motor is counteracted by its aerodynamic penalty? How much range are we willing to give up for extra payload capacity? How do we optimally control battery charging – electrically and thermally – to strike a balance between turnaround time and battery longevity?

Answering these types of questions requires high-caliber computational tools. Zipline is seeking an engineering intern that can understand system-level problem statements, appreciate the tradeoffs between accuracy and computational efficiency, and architect elegant code tools. The outputs of these tools will directly drive critical architectural and operational decisions at the aircraft and fleet level.
